beats.text: Around eighty five to ninety percent of Australia's megafauna went extinct before Europeans arrived.

These include some truly crazy animals, such as Diprotodon, a three tonne wombat relative. Procoptodon, a giant Kangaroo. Megalania, an enormous monitor lizard. And Genyornis, a two hundred kilogram flightless bird.
Most disappeared roughly fifty thousand to forty thousand years ago, after humans had arrived, though how long after is debated. So what caused it?
There are three main explanations. Human hunting, changes to the landscape caused by fire, and climate change.
Burnt eggshell fragments suggest humans collected and cooked the eggs of giant flightless birds, potentially reducing their breeding success.
Climate change may also have contributed, but many of these animals had survived earlier climate fluctuations.
Today, many researchers consider human activity a major driver, although the exact causes are still debated.
